newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt retains small gains, eyes range-trade.
newsitem.headline: German debt retains small gains, eyes range-trade.

text.p: German debt held onto small gains in late trading on Wednesday having spent the session moving in a narrow range.
"The market wants to move higher, but domestic sellers seem to preventing this at the moment," said one Frankfurt-based broker.

By 1511 GMT was trading up six basis points at 101.72 near the top of the session's 101.76-101.54 range while the 10-year cash bond was trading at 102.33, compared with Tuesday's close of 102.29. Dealers said there was strong resistance at 101.73, which Bunds were not able to hold above on Wednesday.

Although the market appears to be eyeing international growth without the imminent fear of renewed inflationary pressures, dealers still said it would take some time for the German bond market to break through the key 101.88 level.
The German market also did not receive joy from the U.S. market where Treasuries opened lower, fearing the prospect of higher interest rates in Japan after a stronger than expected "tankan" report.
Similar fears were not yet materialising in Germany even though some economists have suggested the Bundesbank might need to tighten rates at some time in the autumn or early 1998.
For the next days, dealers said they expected more range-trading, with Bunds swaying between 101.73 and 101.36.
"We will just have to see how the market develops, there is not very much we can predict at the moment," another dealer said.
